business: SEGMENT: PI car accident intake, Pleasanton (Shotland pilot)
prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a couple quick questions so I give the most useful guidance:
- How serious were your injuries (minor strains, broken bones, hospitalization, possible long-term impairment)?
- Do you know who was at fault and whether there’s an insurance claim open?
- Are you looking for someone local in Pleasanton/Alameda County or are you OK with a Bay Area firm?

Meanwhile, here’s practical, reliable guidance so you can pick the right attorney.

Immediate actions (if you haven’t already done them)
- Get and keep medical care records (diagnoses, imaging, bills, treatment notes). Don’t skip treatment — gaps can hurt your claim.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicle damage/scene/injuries, the police report number, witness names/phones, repair estimates.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Note that the usual California statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the date of injury (1 year for claims vs. a government entity). Don’t wait too long.

What kind of lawyer to hire
- A personal injury attorney who focuses on car accidents and bodily injury.
- Preferably someone with experience in Alameda County courts and with local adjusters/defense firms.
- If injuries are severe (catastrophic, permanent, brain/spine), prioritize attorneys who handle catastrophic-injury cases and have trial experience and resources to hire experts.

How to evaluate and choose (step-by-step)
1. Interview 3–5 attorneys or firms. Compare answers and gut feel about communication.
2. Verify credentials: California State Bar license, disciplinary history (www.calbar.ca.gov).
3. Check experience: years handling car-accident cases, number of settlements/trials, examples of past settlements/verdicts (not guaranteed results, but helpful).
4. Confirm fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (common is 33% to 40% if settled before suit; lower if they go to trial or recover). Ask about costs advanced and who pays if you lose.
5. Ask who will do the work (lead attorney vs. paralegals/associates) and how often you’ll get updates.
6. Read client reviews but weigh them against referrals and the lawyer’s substantive answers.

Important questions to ask in the initial consultation
- How many car-accident personal injury cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? Can you give a recent example or result?
- Who in your office will handle day-to-day work on my case?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled? (Contingency %, who advances costs, interest on medical liens)
- How do you communicate (phone, email) and how often will I get updates?
- Do you anticipate needing experts (medical, reconstruction)? Will you hire them?
- What’s your estimate of case value and timeline (rough)?
- Will I have to go to court? If so, what is your trial experience?
- Can you provide references from past clients?
- Do you have conflicts of interest with any involved parties/insurance companies?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount.
- Pressure to sign immediately without answering basic questions or showing a written retainer.
- Lack of written fee agreement or unwillingness to put things in writing.
- Very poor communication during the free consult.

Where to look for attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral service
- California State Bar “Find a Lawyer”
- Local recommendations (friends, doctors)
- Reputable review sites (Avvo, Martindale). Use these as starting points, not proof of quality.

If you want, I can:
- Search for and list 4–6 experienced personal injury/car-accident attorneys or firms in Pleasanton and nearby cities (I’ll include contact info, practice focus, and flagged credentials).
- Draft a short phone script or email you can use when contacting them.
Tell me whether you want local-only results and give any case details you’re comfortable sharing (seriousness of injury, whether the other driver was insured, etc.).
